headline_stat.name: significant negative vs positive circular-linear precession slopes (of 61 candidate place cells)

stated_limitation: confirming phase precession as a population-level phenomenon in this session.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000044 (Grosmark & Buzsaki CA1, Achilles linear-track session) is the canonical dataset for hippocampal theta phase precession.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile, restricted to MazeEpoch, excitatory units filtered, direction-split traversals, and the position sampling-rate metadata bug was caught and verified against epoch duration.
justification.analysis: Correct circular statistics throughout: Rayleigh test for entrainment and Kempter circular-linear regression for precession with a valid permutation null that accounts for the slope-grid maximization.
justification.correctness: Headline numbers (63/89 entrained; 28 negative vs 1 positive precession slopes) are internally consistent between README and figures, statistically sound, and physically possible.
justification.figures: Figures clearly show the effect with labeled units and sample sizes, and precession examples are ranked by correlation strength (the correct criterion), though the fig3 tuning-curve example panel includes some edge-peaking cells.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the evidence with nothing misrepresented, but limitations are noted only implicitly ('in this session') rather than discussed explicitly, placing a genuinely clean result at 3.
justification.verdict: Textbook-correct autonomous demonstration of both theta entrainment and phase precession with clean, well-controlled results; accept.
